## Dispatching — `domain:ui` PM seat (`os-tesla`), R16, 2026-09-12T06:1xZ

Claimed: `os-dev` seat, by the `domain:ui` PM seat (`os-tesla`), R16.

Clause-②: yes

**Clause-② `yes`** on the "not sure ⇒ yes" rule: the fix is inside a pin, but whether making it discriminating requires a testid or marker the panel does not yet publish is not known before the work.

### ⭐ Why this is p2 and not "a flake"

Triage's pivot, adopted verbatim — and it is the transferable part:

> The first assertion is `toHaveLength(1)`; the run where the row never arrived reads **`0`**, and a change that **stops rendering the chip entirely** fails with the **same message**. The two are **indistinguishable from the output**, so this flake **trains the reader to re-run instead of to look** — and that is exactly the path by which a real regression on this marker gets re-run to green.

⇒ the harm is not a wasted CI minute. It is that **this pin has lost its ability to report the thing it guards** — objectui#5178's `via_override` marker.

⛔ Not p1: no production code is involved, `main` is not broken, a solo run is green.

### ⚠️ The trap this card is about, applied to your own fix

⛔ **Do not "fix" it by adding a wait and re-running until green.** The deliverable is a pin whose failure message **distinguishes** "the row did not arrive yet" from "the chip is no longer rendered". If your repaired pin still fails with one message for both causes, it has the same defect in a longer form.

⇒ prove it with an ablation that produces **both** causes separately and shows **different** readings.

## Release — the slice merged, the card was never returned to the queue

PR objectui#9259 merged at 2026-09-12T07:22:25Z carrying `Part of #9158` and ⛔ no closing keyword: a **partial landing**. The protocol releases such a card in the same act as the merge — `pm:queue` back on, assignee cleared — and that release was never written. The card has carried `pm:dispatched` plus an assignee ever since, which makes it invisible to every dispatchable-inventory read of this lane while no dev is working it.

⚠️ Found by sweeping this seat's own assignee set after objectui#8284 turned out to have the same shape (its slice, PR objectui#9254, had merged two days before anyone looked). **Nine cards in this lane were in this state**, this one among them.

⛔ **A state repair, not a verdict on what remains.** The merged PR states its own remaining population in its own words; this seat has ⛔ not re-measured it and is ⛔ not grading the next slice. Whoever claims it reads the PR body and this card's comments first.

State written: one `label-write.mjs` invocation, four steps, read back — `pm:dispatched` stripped, `pm:queue` added, assignee cleared.

## Closing — the residual no longer exists, measured on `main`

⛔ **Not a verdict inherited from the PR.** My own release note (2026-09-14T09:25Z) said this seat had *not* re-measured what remained and that whoever claimed the card reads PR objectui#9259 and these comments first. I claimed it, read them, and measured. This comment is that measurement.

### The defect, as this card states it

> `renderPanel` … awaits `findByTestId('record-approvals-panel')` — the panel SHELL — and the test then asserts `getAllByTestId('via-override-chip')` **synchronously**.

Read at `origin/main` `bbc9dc3`, file blob `7cf0fcf`:

| probe | count | reading |
|---|---|---|
| `await screen.findByTestId(` | **0** | the shell settle is gone from this file entirely |
| `findByTestId('record-approvals-panel')` | 1 | `:26` — **prose** in the docblock, recording what the pin *previously* did |
| `record-approvals-panel` (any) | 2 | `:26` prose + `:163` `queryByTestId` inside `panelSnapshot()`, a **synchronous** diagnostic read that builds the failure text; not a settle |
| `findByText` | 2 | ⭐ the replacement — `settleTimelineRows()` awaits one `findByText` per stubbed actor |

Lit controls carried on purpose: `findByText` = 2 and `record-approvals-panel` = 2 are non-zero **in the same grep pass** that reads 0, so the zero is a reading and not a dead pattern.

### The second half — the one that mattered more

The card's Direction named it: *"the sibling cases in the same file that assert an ABSENCE need the positive settle even more."* Present:

| probe | count |
|---|---|
| `expectMarkerIsLive()` call sites | **3** |
| `POSITIVE CONTROL DEAD` | 2 |

### The discrimination, which is what the card actually asked for

⛔ The card's dispatch forbade "add a wait and re-run until green". The two causes now read in two vocabularies that share no words:

| probe | count |
|---|---|
| `TIMELINE ROWS NEVER ARRIVED` | 3 |
| `VIA_OVERRIDE MARKER REGRESSION` | 2 |

And the property is pinned, not merely argued — `describe('RecordApprovalsPanel — the pin discriminates its two causes (objectui#9158)')` at `:317` carries two tests, `:318` (a withheld flush must read as timing) and `:331` (a settled timeline with no chip must read as marker).

### ⭐ The family audit, verified rather than accepted

PR objectui#9259's acceptance notes claim the sibling pins carry no such defect and that **no card was owed for any of them**. A closing act should not take that on faith, so it was re-derived at `bbc9dc3`:

| file | shell settles | reading |
|---|---|---|
| `RecordApprovalsPanel.approverIdentity.test.tsx` | **0** | all 8 awaits are `waitFor` on the asserted content itself |
| `RecordApprovalsPanel.stepProgressVertical.test.tsx` | **0** | `find*By`/`waitFor` count is 0 — no async settle at all |
| `RecordApprovalsPanel.test.tsx` | 2 (`:157`, `:215`) | both sound — see below |

`:157` settles on the shell **as its own assertion**, then asserts `Waiting on` / `Qian Hua` / `Li Lei` / `· production` / `×2` — every one of them derived from the `pending_approvers` / `pending_approver_names` **props** `renderPanel` passes, so they land in the shell's first commit. Same flush ⇒ the settle is correct.

`:215` is the interesting one, because it is an **absence** assertion (`queryByRole('button', {name: /Send reminder/})` is null) and carries no `expectMarkerIsLive`-style control. It is still sound, and the proof is three lines further down in the same file: `:225` pins that the panel **renders nothing at all** when `requests` is empty. So the shell settle at `:215` is itself the live control — it cannot pass against an empty render, which is precisely the hazard this card's rule 2 names. ⇒ nothing owed, and I am ⛔ not filing a card about it.

### Verdict

Every claim this card makes is repaired on `main`, and the repair exceeds the Direction the card wrote (which asked only for `findAllByTestId` on the chip; what landed makes the two causes *report differently* and controls every absence). No residual, no follow-up slice, no successor card.

⇒ closed as completed, `pm:queue` stripped. PR objectui#9259 said `Part of #9158` because a dev seat never ends a card — the PM does. This is the PM doing it.
